add.issue.comment.md:
Analysis before implementation, 2026-10-29.

**The seed is the smaller half of the core gap.** The store makes news from *state changes* (`transition(old,new)`), but a catalogue feed emits *events*: "this id is new", "this paid model became free". If the price is encoded in the condition state so paid→free produces a news item, then free→paid flips the state back and produces a **"recovered" news item** — which this ticket forbids. And "new" needs the previous catalogue, including ids that have since disappeared; the store deliberately drops any key a source no longer returns, so conditions cannot be that memory.

**Proposal — a source-owned memory dict.** Let a source persist a small dict through the store (`sources[id].memory`, written atomically with the rest of the state) and receive it in `check(now, memory)`. Empty memory means first run, so the seed needs no separate flag. The feed keeps `{model-id: {free: bool}}` there, which answers all three rules at once: novelty against the stored ids, paid→free as a stored-price comparison, free→paid silent while still updating the stored price, and a disappeared model staying in memory so its return is not "new". Reusable by the other catalogue feeds (Traveller players, world news).

**Ranking, my recommendation.** A config list of family/route substrings is the human's own judgement, needs no new data and matches the "minimax / space bunny" example; the modelbench can join later as a second signal (a model with a ledger row outranks an unknown), but its grades are per-episode permissions, not a rank, so it cannot be the only source. Metadata is not a quality ranking.

**Not blocked either way:** the two catalogue readers (`opencode models` CLI, OpenRouter `/api/v1/models`) and their parsers.
add.issue.comment.author: G3EADTNG57JJEEP7B2C7FASVA7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `6782c5d` on master (direct, under the Marduk merge rule).

**Core — a source may keep memory.** `sources[id].memory` is a dict the store round-trips with the rest of the state and hands to `check(now, memory=None)`; empty on the first run, unchanged by a failed run. That is what makes an event feed expressible: a catalogue's news is "an id appeared", which the transition rules cannot carry (a state flip back would read as a recovery), and the drop-unknown-keys rule cannot remember a model that left the catalogue. SPEC R4, R15 and D13.

**The feed — `kind: "models"`.** Reads the console (`opencode models`) and OpenRouter (`/api/v1/models`); the console's prices are joined from the model database (`models.dev`) because the CLI lists ids only. A model is identified by its id with a leading `openrouter/` removed, so the console's OpenRouter route and OpenRouter itself are one entry. The first run seeds (587 models, 32 free on this machine) and announces nothing. After that: a new id is one `info` item; a paid→free model that matches `powerful` is one; free→paid is silent and updates the memory; a disappeared model stays in memory and its return is not "new"; prices are cached for 6 h. `powerful` is the user's list of id substrings — the live config starts with the two examples, `minimax` and `space-bunny`, and is the human's to extend (space-bunny is not in the current console list).

**Verified.** 107 tests in the marduk suite (15 for the feed, 2 for the memory round-trip and the failed-run rule), `xlint tools/marduk` clean, a live `--once` green on site, apt and models, and the four running panels restarted. The repository runner still fails on `dev/xcsv/tests` from the human's uncommitted rewrite — pre-existing and unrelated.
add.issue.comment.author: G3EADTNG57JJEEP7B2C7FASVA7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `d6b2a51` on master (direct, under the Marduk merge rule).

**Where the data is.** The game keeps `data/users.json` (the player list) and `data/users/<name>.json` per player; `props.created` is the join time and `props.last_active` the last-seen time. The panel's host reads the directory directly — no export needed, and the configured `data_path` carries the location because it is machine-specific. A broken player file is skipped rather than failing the feed.

**The feed — `kind: "players"`.** The first run seeds the last-active times and announces nothing. After that: a player not in memory is one `info` item ("new player: X"); a player whose last-active time advanced by more than `absence_days` (default 14, the ticket's "start with a value") is one item naming the days away. A player idle for a day is not news, and a player who disappears from the list stays in memory, so a return is measured against the last time they were actually seen. Options: `data_path` (required), `absence_days`, `interval_seconds` (default 300), `stale_after_seconds`.

**Verified.** 115 tests in the marduk suite (8 for this feed), `xlint tools/marduk` clean, live `--once` green with site, apt, models and players, seeded against the real data (`Xonok`, `testuser`), and the four running panels restarted.

edit.description.md:
## Goal

Tell the human when a new player joins Traveller, or when someone comes back after a long absence, without watching the game by hand.

## Corrected premise (2026-10-29)

The `Space-Traveller/data/users/*` files on this machine are **test accounts**; the real server is on another machine. A source that reads local files cannot serve this goal — the first attempt did exactly that and was reverted (`d6b2a51` → `053694f`), and it is out of the live config. The feed needs a hook from the real server.

**The hook must be safe to expose.** A credential-free player **count** is acceptable — how many accounts exist is not sensitive. Names, per-player activity, and anything that identifies a person are not. So the first increment can only say "a player joined" when the count grows; a return after an absence needs either an anonymous event from the server or the human's ruling on what may be disclosed.

## Scope

- A server-side, credential-free endpoint (or a small file the server writes) that the panel can read.
- The panel source emits one `info` item for a count increase, with the count and the time; no identity.
- Returns after a long absence need a second signal; settle its disclosure before building it.

## Open

- What the server exposes and where: an endpoint, a log, or a small status file.
- Whether returns can be reported at all without disclosing identities.
- The absence threshold if a per-player signal is allowed.

add.issue.name: modelbench: the newsroom episode — find and aggregate news

edit.description.md:
## Goal

A modelbench episode for the finding half of the news pipeline: given a week of feed items, select the stories worth evaluating and merge outlets covering the same event. It does **not** judge whether a story is true; validity is a later stage.

## Shape

- `episodes/newsroom/data/items.json`: a corpus of feed items with ids and sources.
- The model writes `digest.json`: at most eight items, each with corpus `ids`, a `title` and a `why`.
- `check.py` measures grounding (ids exist, no duplicates), aggregation (one event across outlets is one item with all its ids), recall of the seeded stories, and noise-only items. The corpus hash is a guard.
- A `newsroom` scope manifest keeps the corpus, brief and checker off-limits.

## Acceptance

The untouched episode fails and every guard passes; a digest built from the seeded stories passes every case; splitting one event fails aggregation; a noise-only item fails precision. The checker must not test factual validity.

add.issue.comment.md:

edit.description.md:
**What.** A harness that runs `xprompt` against small, deterministic task fixtures and records raw traces plus a generated ledger. Separate from `tools/modelbench/`; no episodes or gates are shared.

**Design constraints (from `plans/local-model-benchmark.md`).**
- Each task ships a fixture, a prompt, enabled tools, and a deterministic `check.py`. Every checker is validated twice before use: a reference solution must pass, a deliberately broken solution must fail.
- Runs happen in a fresh sandbox copy; the checker is run by the harness, never trusted from the model.
- One JSONL record per run: model tag, task, repeat, xprompt version, effective options, exit code, stdout, turns, tokens, prefill/generation timing, tool-call path (native vs parsed), checker result and reason, final sandbox state.
- Raw traces persist in `library/ai/local-models/runs/<wave>/`; ledger regenerated from them; `bench_version` hashes tasks + runner so an instrument change is visible.
- No LLM judge in pass/fail. Secondary labels (format-clean, verified) are deterministic too.

**Acceptance.** Pilot runs on 3 models complete; every checker passes its self-check; ledger `--check` is idempotent.

**Why.** The local-model benchmark drives `xprompt` as its transport, so the tool must report enough to measure without a separate API client, and must provide the tools the measured workloads need. All changes additive and backwards-compatible.

**Required.**
1. `--json` (or `--stats`): machine-readable result on stdout — content, turns, per-turn tool calls, whether each call came from native `tool_calls` or content parsing, and Ollama's own metrics (`prompt_eval_count`, `prompt_eval_duration`, `eval_count`, `eval_duration`, `load_duration`, `total_duration`). 2. `--option key=value` (repeatable): pass through to Ollama `options` — `temperature`, `seed`, `num_ctx`, `num_gpu`, `num_thread`, `num_predict`, `top_k`, `top_p`, `repeat_penalty`. This is what makes parameter sweeps possible without baking a model tag per combination.
3. `--host URL` and honour `OLLAMA_HOST`: the port is hard-coded to `localhost:11434`, so a second experimental server (different `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS`/`NUM_PARALLEL`) cannot be driven without restarting the main service.
4. `--write` tool (path, content): the companion to `read`. Without it an editing task can only be done through bash heredocs, which measures shell quoting rather than coding. Keep it sandbox-neutral like `bash` — it writes wherever the path says, under the caller's cwd by default.

**Minor.** Remove the unreachable duplicate block in `execute_tool` and the unused `socket_timeout_exc`.

**Tests.** `XLib/tools/test/`, including option passthrough, host selection, JSON shape, write tool, and exit codes.

edit.description.md:
**Why.** The local-model benchmark's acceptance has an operational half the task suite does not cover: per-model prefill/generation speed, memory when resident, and whether several models answer concurrently without stress.

**Add** `tools/localbench/ops.py` (additive, no change to run.py or the task suite):

- `--models m1,m2,... --out DIR`: for each model, warm it, then measure prefill and generation at roughly 100 / 1,000 / 4,000 prompt tokens with `num_predict=32`, 3 repeats, temperature 0. add.issue.name: localbench: 32k needle prompt hits argv limit; summarize incident fact is too literal

edit.description.md:
Two instrument defects found by the 2026-10-31 probe wave (traces: Agents `library/ai/local-models/runs/2026-10-31-probe/`).

**1. needle/p32k cannot run: the prompt exceeds the OS argv limit.**
`run.py` passes the task prompt as `--prompt <text>`. The p32k fixture is ~128 KB, over Linux's 128 KB single-argument limit (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`), so the run dies with `OSError: [Errno 7] Argument list too long` before xprompt starts. p16k (~67 KB) fits. The 32k rung of the needle family is therefore unmeasurable for every model, and the failure looks like a crash rather than a task result.

Fix: add `--prompt-file PATH` to xprompt (read the prompt from disk), and have `run.py` use it when `task.json` names a `prompt_file`. Do **not** remove p32k: the task is sound and only the transport is short.

**2. summarize/incident requires a literal phrase, so a paraphrase fails.**
The checker requires the exact string `resolved by rollback`. Four models (gemma4:e4b, cogito:8b, qwen2.5-coder-7b-cpu-opt, qwen2.5:14b…) wrote *"resolved by rolling back to the prior release"* — the fact, in another word form — and were graded `ok: false`. Only qwen2.5-3b-opt happened to write "Resolved by rollback" and passed. This measures wording, not capability.

Fix: make the last fact an alternatives list (`rollback` / `rolling back` / `rolled back`) and re-run the cell under a new `bench_version`; stored rows keep their old result.

Both are task/instrument changes, so a new `bench_version`; no stored row is rewritten.

add.issue.name: localbench: needle/p32k is 16,386 tokens — shorter than p16k, so the 32k rung is mislabelled

edit.description.md:
**Found by the 2026-10-31 verdict wave** (rows: Agents `library/ai/local-models/runs/2026-10-31-verdict/`).

Ollama's `prompt_eval_count` for the needle fixtures, first (cold) run of each case:

| Case | Fixture bytes | Prompt tokens |
|---|---|---|
| p4k | 19,470 | 4,224 |
| p8k | 38,868 | 8,402 |
| p16k | 77,649 | 16,749 |
| p32k | 155,217 | **16,386** |

**The 32k rung is not 32k tokens, and it is actually shorter than the 16k rung.** The fixture doubles in bytes but the token count falls, so the family's stated maximum (32k) overstates what was measured by roughly 2×.

**Cause (hypothesis, to confirm while fixing):** the filler is generated by cycling a 30-word vocabulary in repeated paragraphs (`tasks/needle/*/p32k.txt`), so BPE merges long repeated runs and the chars-per-token ratio rises with length. The 155 KB fixture is still over Linux's `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`, which is why the argv failure was real — the transport fix in `9PDCHD4` was correct; the fixture's *token* length is the separate defect.

**Fix:** generate the filler from a varied vocabulary (or a long prose source) so chars-per-token stays near 4, then assert the token counts against the rung names; alternatively name the rungs by measured tokens and add a true 32k rung. The task is otherwise sound (reference passes, broken fails).

**Effect:** task change — a new `bench_version`; stored rows are not rewritten. The 2026-10-31 needle verdict rows stand as the 4k/8k/17k/16k evidence they are, and a re-run gives the real 32k rung.

add.issue.name: localbench ops: speed repeats hit Ollama's prompt cache, so prefill tok/s is inflated

edit.description.md:
**Found while preparing the 2026-10-31 ops run.** `ops.speed_for_model()` sends the same `human_filler(target)` prompt `REPS` (3) times per length. Ollama keeps the prompt-prefix KV cache for a loaded model, so repeats 2 and 3 are cache hits: `prompt_eval_count` collapses and `prefill_s` collapses with it. The reported median is then `[full, tiny, tiny] -> tiny`, i.e. the prefill tok/s number is inflated by the cache, not measured.

**Evidence:** in the verdict wave the same effect showed on identical needle prompts — `needle/p32k` first run 12.2 s / 11.2 s prefill, repeats 1.0 s / 0.1 s prefill, same prompt and `prompt_tokens` (Agents `library/ai/local-models/runs/2026-10-31-verdict/`).

**Fix:** make each repeat's prompt textually unique at the **start** (a per-repeat nonce line), which invalidates the prefix cache and forces a real prefill. `human_filler(target_tokens, tag=None)` prepends `Request <tag>.` when a tag is given; `speed_for_model` passes a per-repeat tag. `COUNT_PROMPT` still ends the prompt.

**Effect:** ops-only; `ops.py` is not hashed into `bench_version`, so no stored row changes and no capability wave needs re-running. The concurrency calls use one tiny identical prompt and are unaffected (all calls are cached equally, which is the intended comparison).

**Also record on the model pages:** the prefill speeds in the plan's manual table (2026-10-30) were measured with short prompts, so they are cold and unaffected; the ops suite's numbers are the ones this bug would have corrupted.

add.issue.name: localbench selftest leaks all but the last scenario's temp directory

edit.description.md:
Found while reviewing `9PDCHD4` (recorded there, not fixed): `tools/localbench/selftest.py` creates one temp directory per scenario and calls `shutil.rmtree(td)` **once, after the scenario loop**, so only the last scenario's temp dir is removed and the rest leak into `/tmp`.

**Fix:** remove each scenario's temp dir in a `finally` (or use `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` per scenario).

Cosmetic, but it means a selftest run leaves ~2 directories behind each time, and a leak on a CI host would accumulate.

add.issue.name: localbench ops: per-model option/placement, so the concurrency arm can pin the CPU models

edit.description.md:

edit.title.name: localbench: an oversized needle prompt is silently truncated to half the model's context, and the p32k rung is scored from it

edit.description.md:
**Found by the 2026-10-31 verdict wave** (rows: Agents `library/ai/local-models/runs/2026-10-31-verdict/`).

Ollama's `prompt_eval_count` for the needle fixtures, first (cold) run of each case:

| Case | Fixture bytes | Reported prompt tokens | True prompt tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| p4k | 19,470 | 4,224 | 4,224 |
| p8k | 38,868 | 8,402 | 8,402 |
| p16k | 77,649 | 16,749 | 16,749 |
| p32k | 155,217 | **16,386** | **33,427** |

**Corrected cause (measured 2026-10-31):** the ticket first blamed BPE merging repeated filler, and that is wrong — a fixed tokenizer does not change its merges by document. The p32k fixture is ~33,400 tokens and is fine. `qwen2.5-3b-32k` has a 32,768-token context; ollama **clamps the task's requested `num_ctx=65536` to the model maximum and, when the prompt is longer, keeps only the last half of the context** (16,384 tokens plus the question). - the README documents the ollama behaviour.

The 3B's p32k rows stand as truncated 16k evidence, and the 3B's needle capability is measured to ~17k only — a 32k rung cannot run on a 32k-context model at all (the fixture is 33.4k). edit.description.md:
**Found on the 2026-10-31 pinned re-run** (`runs/2026-10-31-ops2/concurrency.json`). With placement pinned correctly (`qwen2.5-3b-32k` `size_vram 2.08 GB`, the two CPU models `size_vram 0`), the 26B's concurrent walls came back at **0.92–0.95 s** and the 3B at **0.16–0.27 s**. A 26B does not answer in 0.9 s.

The concurrency arm sends the same string — `Reply with exactly: OK` — for every call, solo and concurrent. Ollama keeps the prompt-prefix KV cache, so every call after the first is prefilled for free; and the answer is two tokens, so generation is not a measurement either. The arm is measuring cache hits and scheduling noise.

The speed arm already got a unique prompt per repeat in `N3CBQWB`; the concurrency arm never did. The earlier manual arm's 20 s 26B solo did real work and its numbers are not comparable with this JSON.

**Fix:** make every concurrency call unique (a tag in the prompt), ask for a fixed non-trivial generation (the 1–40 list, `num_predict=64`) so generation is real, and record each call's `error` and content so a failed call cannot be reported as a fast one. Re-run the arm.

add.issue.name: localbench extract/invoice: total compared as a string rejects 1240.5

edit.description.md:
**Defect:** `tools/localbench/tasks/extract/invoice/check.py` compares the `total` field as a string and rejects a correct answer whose trailing zero is not written.

`normalize_total()` strips everything but digits and dots, so the expected `"1240.50"` is compared against `str(1240.5)` → `"1240.5"`. **The prompt says nothing about a two-decimal string**, and the function's own shape (`re.sub(r"[^0-9.]", "", …)`) says it intends to tolerate formatting — it just does not tolerate the float form of a number it accepts as a string.

**Measured impact on the corpus:** of 72 `extract/invoice` rows in `library/ai/local-models/ledger.jsonl`, **21 fail only on this** and 6 more are unparseable. The 21 span 11 models and cost each of them 1–2 rows of `extract` — e.g. `ornith:9b` 4/6 → 6/6, `qwen3.5:4b` 4/6 → 6/6, `ministral-3:8b` 2/6 → 4/6, `llama3.1:8b` 2/6 → 4/6. `extract` was therefore reading as a discriminator when most of the difference was the checker.

**Fix:** compare numerically (`Decimal`) in both `ok` and `contract_clean`, keeping the existing tolerance for `EUR`, commas and whitespace. Also delete the dead first `contract_clean` block in the same function — it is immediately overwritten, which is what makes the real rule hard to read.

**Consequences, stated up front:** `check.py` is part of the hashed task set, so `bench_version` moves and every future row carries the new one. Historical rows keep the version they were measured under; `ledger.py --check` will report the 21 rows as disagreements, which is the instrument behaving as designed (a checker change surfaces rather than silently re-grades). The screening cut decisions do not change: `codellama:7b` (2/6) and `lfm2.5-thinking:1.2b` (0/6) stay below the bar even with their invoice rows corrected.

**Scope: this ticket only.** The `classify` family's whole-pool failure was checked in the same pass and is **not** a checker defect — the reference is in the presented (shuffled) order, which is the natural reading of "one label per line", and the failures are real (21 lines instead of 20, ranges substituted for labels, repetition loops).

add.issue.name: taskview/taskupdate/taskboard: a task queued behind another is hidden until that task resolves (`--queued-on`)

edit.description.md:
A task that cannot start yet was still shown in the pane and counted in every metric, so the numbers included work that was waiting on something else.

**What changed**
- `taskupdate`: a tenth CSV column `queued_on` holds the task id this task waits on (or empty). `add` and `update` take `--queued-on <id>`, and `--queued-on none` clears it; `show` prints it. Every write path carries the column forward, so an unrelated `--due` or `--title` cannot silently drop the link.
- `taskview`: a task whose `queued_on` target exists and is neither done nor cancelled is hidden from the pane and excluded from the counts — as an unresolved dependency, not as work filtered out by this view. `--show-queued` reveals them. A target that does not exist does not hide the task, so a stale id fails open.
- `taskboard`: `set_due` copies `queued_on` forward with the other stored fields, so editing a due date does not break the chain.
- `tools/taskview/SPEC.md`: the data model records ten columns and the read rule that makes the addition backward compatible — a row with nine columns reads `queued_on` as empty (R36).

**Why no store migration:** the store is append-only and read row-by-row, so old rows need no rewrite; the column is empty for every task that predates it.

**Verified**
- taskview: 166 tests pass (`dev/xtest/xtest.py tools/taskview/test`), including the updated R32 column count.
- taskboard: 191 tests pass, including R11 (every stored field is copied to the new row) now asserting `queued_on`.
- `xlint` clean on every touched file.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: committed to `master` as `7ae5ee6` and pushed. The change is non-breaking — a nine-column row reads `queued_on` as empty — so it skips `Done` and is closed with the commit.

What landed: `taskupdate` writes the column from `--queued-on` on add and update, clears it on `none`, and preserves it on every other write path; `taskview` hides a selected task whose target exists and is unresolved and counts it as an unresolved dependency rather than as work the view filtered out, with `--show-queued` to see the set; `taskboard.set_due` preserves the column; `tools/taskview/SPEC.md` records the tenth column and the backward-compatible read rule.

The visible half is the pane and the metrics: a task can now name what it waits for, and it stops taking space and counting until that task is done or cancelled. A missing target fails open, so a stale id cannot hide work forever.

Verification: taskview 166 tests and taskboard 191 tests pass; `xlint` clean on every touched file.

add.issue.name: localbench ops: add the sustained stress arm (swap, OOM, latency drift)

edit.description.md:
The plan's operational suite specifies a 10-minute sustained mixed-call run on the resident set, but `ops.py` only has `--models` and `--concurrency`. The concurrency arm proves three short calls overlap; it cannot show whether the set stays healthy under continued load, which is the "without undue stress" half of the definition of done.

Add `--stress m1,m2,m3 --stress-minutes N`: warm the set, then run rounds of concurrent calls on a production-shaped prompt mix (~100/500/1000 tokens, unique tag per call to defeat the prompt cache), recording per-call wall time, load average, `pswpin`/`pswpout`, `oom_kill` and `MemAvailable`/`SwapFree`. Write `stress.json` with the raw calls, samples and a per-model summary (calls, failures, median wall, first/last-third drift, residency after).

Acceptance: `--models` and `--concurrency` unchanged; a `--stress` smoke on one model works; `test_ops.py` green; the first real run recorded under `library/ai/local-models/runs/2026-11-01-ops-stress/`.

add.issue.comment.md: **Solution:** fixed in `21bcd34` (PR #135). `--model-option MODEL:KEY=VALUE` is repeatable, wins over the shared set, and the effective options are recorded per model in the speed and concurrency JSON. The remaining condition — the concurrency arm re-run with the pins — has since landed: `runs/2026-10-31-ops-working-set/` (3B 2.08 GB VRAM, both CPU models at `size_vram 0`, worst inflation 1.81×, aggregate 14.3 s against 17.9 s summed, no swap/OOM), and the new `--stress` arm uses the same per-model options (`runs/2026-11-01-ops-stress/`). Closing.
